changes.text: 台谏请停修京通铁路；张之洞的议奏则排出修路之利的次序、列成条目，并把一条南北线路的北段、南段分给督抚。传文在「得旨報可」之后，接着记他调任湖广，并奏开炼铁厂「資路用」；本传没有记这条线路的修筑经过。

The censors asked to halt the Beijing-Tongzhou railway. Zhang Zhidong's memorial ranked the benefits of building railways, set them out as numbered items, and assigned the northern and southern sections of a north-south line to governors-general and a governor. After "approved by rescript," the biography goes on to record his transfer to Huguang and his petition to open an ironworks to supply the railway; this biography does not record how the line itself was built.
要不要修京通铁路，朝中有了争执。《清史稿·张之洞传》记：「會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦」。海军衙门主张修，台谏（负责进言、弹劾的言官）争陈铁路之害、请停办。传文紧接着又记了另外两种主张：「翁同龢等請試修邊地，便用兵；徐會灃請改修德州濟寧路，利漕運」，其后录有张之洞的议奏。至于台谏所说的害具体是哪几条、海军衙门的理由为何，传文都没有记。

The proposed Beijing-Tongzhou railway drew opposition at court. The Draft History of the Qing records it this way (here and throughout, quotations from the Chinese are our own translations): "When the Naval Office petitioned to build the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, the censors pressed the harms of railways and asked that the project be halted." The Naval Office stood for building; the censors - the court's officials charged with remonstrance and impeachment - pressed the harms and asked for a stop. The biography then records two further proposals: Weng Tonghe and others asked to try building in the frontier regions, for ease of moving troops; Xu Huifeng asked to build a Dezhou-Jining line instead, for the benefit of grain transport. After that it records Zhang Zhidong's memorial. Which harms the censors meant, and what reasons the Naval Office gave, the biography does not record.
本文传主张之洞针对这几种主张上了一份议奏，其中明确排出了目标次序：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之」。目标的轻重被明明白白摆上桌面——作者认为，这个排序是这篇议奏最容易被略过、也最见功夫的地方。

Zhang Zhidong, the subject of this biography, answered these proposals with a memorial that set out an explicit ranking of goals: "In building a railway, the greatest benefit lies in moving local goods and enriching the people's livelihood; raising troops and forwarding supplies come second." The relative weight of the goals is laid plainly on the table. In the author's view, that ranking is the easiest thing to skim past in this memorial, and the place where the real craft sits.
一种解释是，这个排序是有意为之：台谏争的是「鐵路之害」，而翁同龢等已以「便用兵」为由请试修边地；若先论兵事，便与这一主张在同一题目上相争，争执或许更烈（作者推测，传文未载）；把民生摆在前头，等于把辩论引到“土货通不通、民生厚不厚”这类可以逐条说的题目上。作者推断这只是顺序上的策略，传文并未写他这样排的理由。

One reading is that the ranking is deliberate. The censors were arguing "the harms of railways," and Weng Tonghe and others had already asked to try building in the frontier regions for ease of moving troops; had he opened on military matters, he would have been contesting the same ground as that proposal, and the fight might have grown hotter (the author's conjecture; the biography does not say so). Placing livelihoods first steers the debate onto ground where points can be settled one by one - do local goods flow, do livelihoods thicken. The author infers this is tactics in the ordering; the biography records no reason of his own for the sequence.
议奏逐条列「利」，传文留下了编号：利一到利七，每条一两句，最后一条是「海上用兵，漕運無梗，利七」；议奏随即提出「有此七利，分段分年成之」。这组「利」是他自己列举的理由，不是独立核算过的数字。

The memorial works through a numbered list of benefits, and the biography preserves the numbering: benefit one through benefit seven, each a sentence or two. The last reads: "Should war come by sea, grain transport will not be obstructed - benefit seven." The memorial then proposes: "With these seven benefits, let it be completed section by section, year by year." These are reasons he assembled himself, not figures from any independent accounting.
结果是「得旨報可，遂有移楚之命」。朝廷准了这份奏请，随后有调他赴湖广之命。需要说清楚的是，「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工；张之洞本传没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁，只在其后记他奏开炼铁厂「資路用」；同卷《王文韶传》记有京汉铁路兴筑，是否即此线，本文不作断定，也不替他补写这些细节。

The outcome: "The memorial received an approving rescript, and there followed the order transferring him to Huguang." The throne approved the request, and an order sending him to Huguang followed. Be clear: "approved by rescript" means the memorial was accepted, not that work began. Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the line he proposed; it goes on only to record his petition for an ironworks to supply the railway. The biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter records the building of the Beijing-Hankou railway; whether that is this line, this article does not decide, and it will not supply the missing details.
传文对他有一句评语：「蒞官所至，必有興作。務宏大，不問費多寡」。传文同时记他任疆寄数十年，「及卒，家不增一畝」。一种解释是，这句话与前面那份编号清单出自同一种风格——敢开大摊子，也肯把摊子一条条写出来；至于花费，评语说他不问多寡，传文并未举出具体用款数字；按「家不增一畝」这一限定，“不问花费”不宜读作为私谋利。

The biography passes a verdict on him: "Wherever he took office, he had works begun. He aimed at the grand, and did not ask how much it cost." It also records that after decades as a provincial official, "at his death, his family had not gained a single mu of land." One reading: that verdict and the numbered list share the same style - bold enough to open big undertakings, willing to write each out item by item. As for spending, the verdict says he did not ask the amount; the biography gives no figures. Read with the qualifier about his family's land, "did not ask how much it cost" should not be taken as spending for private gain.
作者的一种读法是，这份议奏包含四个部分：排目标次序（通土货、厚民生最大，征兵转饷次之），列逐条的「利」并编号（共七条），提出「分段分年成之」，落实到官职（北路直隶总督、南路湖广总督、河南巡抚为副）。作者认为，这样写可能把争论从“有没有害”引向“这些逐条的「利」成不成立、这三位督抚之职扛不扛得动”。

One reading is that the memorial has four components: a ranking of goals (moving goods and enriching livelihoods greatest, raising troops and forwarding supplies next); a numbered, item-by-item list of benefits, seven in all; a proposal to complete the line section by section, year by year; and responsibility assigned to offices (north to the Governor-General of Zhili, south to the Governor-General of Huguang, the Governor of Henan as deputy). In the author's view, writing it this way may steer the argument away from "is it harmful" toward "do these itemized benefits hold, and can these three offices carry them."
作者提出的替代选择（传文没有记载，属反事实）：议奏已主张「分段分年成之」，但没有先试修一小段、看运量与扰民程度再定其余各段的设计；另一种做法是把「利」逐条配上可核对的口径，让反对者逐条检验，这在议奏中也未见。这两种设计是作者提出的比较项，不是议奏里的内容。

Alternatives the author offers (absent from the biography, therefore counterfactual): the memorial already proposes completing the line section by section, year by year, but it has no design for building a short stretch first and letting freight volumes and the degree of disruption decide the rest; another option would be to attach a checkable yardstick to each "benefit," so opponents could test them one by one, and that too does not appear in the memorial. Both designs are comparison items the author raises, not part of the memorial.
写一份提案或评审材料时，可以借用这份议奏的顺序：开头不急着罗列优劣，先交代哪个目标最重、哪个其次，把轻重写在最前面；随后把支持的理由分条编号，像那七条编号的“利”一样，每一条都留给读者去追问“成不成立”。

When drafting a proposal or a review document, you can borrow this memorial's order: rather than opening with a list of pros and cons, state up front which goal weighs most and which comes next; then number the supporting reasons one by one, like those seven numbered benefits, leaving each open to the reader's challenge: "does this hold?"
再次，张之洞本传没有记议奏所提线路的工期、用款、拆迁，只在其后记他奏开炼铁厂「資路用」；同卷《王文韶传》有京汉铁路兴筑的记载，是否同一线路无法确定，本文不替他补写；「得旨報可」只是准奏，不等于已经开工，更不等于办成。本文也不把原文没有的公元年份换算出来，更不会说他事先知道结果——他写下那些「利」的时候，看到的只是清单，不是成绩单。

Third, Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations for the proposed line; it goes on only to record his petition for an ironworks to supply the railway. The biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter records the building of the Beijing-Hankou railway, but whether it is the same line cannot be determined, and this article does not fill in the gaps. "Approved by rescript" is approval, not the start of work, still less a finished line. This article also converts no Common Era years the original does not have, and will not say he knew the outcome in advance: when he wrote those numbered benefits, what lay before him was a checklist, not a report card.
本文所据仅为《清史稿·张之洞传》一份传文，无第二种记载对照；议奏文字按史书所录转述，未必是逐字原话；「利」为他自列的理由，非独立核算；张之洞本传未记工期、用款、拆迁，同卷《王文韶传》所记京汉铁路兴筑是否即此线，未作断定；「得旨報可」仅为准奏，不等于开工；不换算公元年份，亦不假定他事先知道结果。

This article rests on one source, the biography of Zhang Zhidong in the Draft History of the Qing, with no second record for comparison. The memorial text is reported as the historians recorded it and may not be verbatim; the "benefits" are reasons he listed himself, not independent figures; Zhang's own biography records no schedule, outlay, or relocations, and whether the Beijing-Hankou railway recorded in the biography of Wang Wenshao in the same chapter is this line is left undecided; "approved by rescript" means approval only, not the start of work. No Common Era years are converted, and no foreknowledge of the outcome is assumed.
